The largest point size whose predicted width still fits a target

Source: R/render-latex.R
apa_size_for_width.Rd

The inverse of `apa_latex_natural_width()`. That function contains a round-UP step (every column's content is rounded up to the nearest 0.01 in before summing), so it is not exactly invertible in closed form: two adjacent sizes can round to the same summed width, and the naive algebraic inverse (solving the un-rounded linear formula for `size`) can land fractionally past where the ROUNDED forward function actually still fits. `apa_size_for_width()` is defined as the largest size, no bigger than `APA_LATEX_MAX_FONT_SIZE` (12 pt – see that constant: neither APA's own body type nor the model's own measurement ever goes above it), whose predicted width – by `apa_latex_natural_width()`, the exact same function every other caller uses, not the un-rounded approximation used only to seed the search – still fits `target`. It gets there by solving the un-rounded formula once (closed form, no re-measurement of the table's text), clamping that estimate to the [`APA_LATEX_MIN_EMITTABLE_SIZE`, `APA_LATEX_MAX_FONT_SIZE`] range a font size can be emitted in at all, then walking the clamped estimate down in 0.001 pt steps, re-checking against the real (rounded) formula, until it fits.

Usage

apa_size_for_width(plan, target, content_12 = NULL)

Arguments

plan

a display plan, from `apa_display_plan()`.

target

target width in inches.

content_12

optional per-column content vector already measured by `apa_latex_content_at_12()`. Supplying it is what lets Task 9's ladder make its whole decision from ONE font measurement: that measurement runs flextable's `autofit()` and costs about 0.66 s on a 14-column table, and the ladder needs the same vector for the width at 10 pt, for the solve, and for the achieved-fit re-check. It must be the vector measured from `plan` – it is not a way to price one table against another's columns.

Value

numeric point size, in `[APA_LATEX_MIN_EMITTABLE_SIZE, APA_LATEX_MAX_FONT_SIZE]`.

There is no legibility floor (D7b)

This function used to stop at the flextable fitter's 5 pt floor, which meant a table needing less was returned at 5 pt and CLIPPED. D7b makes 6 pt a warning threshold and never a hard stop, so the walk now continues below 5 pt – and below 1 pt – to whatever size actually fits, bottoming out only at `APA_LATEX_MIN_EMITTABLE_SIZE` (**0.1 pt**, the smallest size a rendered table was measured to be set at rather than substituted; see that constant, and do NOT restore the 0.5 pt figure an earlier draft of this sentence carried – 0.5 pt was assumed and the measurement disproved it).

The invariant, and the one case that genuinely cannot fit

`apa_latex_natural_width(plan, apa_size_for_width(plan, target)) <= target` now holds for every `target` a table can be made to fit at all. It cannot hold when NO size fits, and that case is real rather than theoretical, because part of the width does not scale with the type size: `\tabcolsep` contributes `(4n - 4)` pt whatever the font, and every column's content is rounded UP to the next 0.01 in, so an `n`-column table is never narrower than `0.01*n + (4n - 4)/72.27 + APA_LATEX_WIDTH_MARGIN_IN`. When `target` is below that, this function returns `APA_LATEX_MIN_EMITTABLE_SIZE` and the predicted width exceeds `target`. A caller that needs to know whether the fit actually succeeded – Task 9's ladder, deciding whether to warn – must check `apa_latex_natural_width(plan, result) <= target` itself; this function's return value alone does not carry that information.
